Done. The endgame crowd-join package is built, tested and live on tomorrow's Cup book since 8:57 pm (restart kept every order, 593 rows came back). ORLY finished +36 and was left alone. What changed, all pre-race, lagging sides only: 1) A side the arrival rule stopped can look again when the crowd moves down and leaves room under our lowest ask, at most twice per stage and 30 min apart. Today Love and Kvapil stopped once in the morning and were never looked at again. 2) Once the crowd is 70% in, a lagging side may price down to 5 cents under fair instead of 2, still inside the concession budget. 3) In that same endgame, dead rows above the crowd get trimmed every 30 min, keeping the closest level, so the room goes to a row that can actually sell. 4) The pre-race take reads three bid levels instead of one, never more than 5 cents under fair, same budget. Today 2 contracts at the top bid blocked a take on Love with 127 more right under it. 5) A plain status line every 10 min for each lagging side. On Love: no, we did not sell him too cheap or too many. Zero Love sold before green and he was never the biggest pile (713 vs 934). He was frozen by the one-row stop and the dead rows. One thing you need to know: the first re-arm fired right away on Byron (the only lagging side for tomorrow) and posted 1,049 at the crowd's 4 cents. That pushed his resting total past the backstop cap, and the existing cap rule then removed 9 old Byron rows at 7 to 14 cents (about 1,090 contracts sitting 3 to 10 cents above the crowd) and shrank one. That rule has done the same about 20 times this week on the three Homestead books, this was the biggest. Byron's worst case stays inside the backstop. My recommendation: leave it. Rows that far above the crowd give way to a row at the price that sells, which is what you asked for tonight.
